record.title: The logarithmic-logarithmic expansion conjecture for group representations
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\rho$ be a nontrivial irreducible unitary representation of $G$. A subset $S\subset G$ is **$\varepsilon$-expanding with respect to $\rho$** when

$$
\left\|\frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{g\in S}\rho(g)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq 1-\varepsilon.
$$

**The logarithmic-logarithmic expansion conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant $C_\varepsilon$ such that, for every finite group $G$ and every nontrivial irreducible unitary representation $\rho$, there is a subset $S\subset G$ with

$$
|S|\leq C_\varepsilon\log\log|G|
$$

that is $\varepsilon$-expanding with respect to $\rho$. The conjecture asserts that the doubly logarithmic upper bound arising in the paper cannot be improved in general; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Yufei Zhao, “Group representations that resist worst-case sampling”, arXiv:1705.04675 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.04675

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2017).

record.title: Amit's conjecture on word-map fibers in finite nilpotent groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite nilpotent group, let $\overline{x}$ denote a tuple of variables, and let $w(\overline{x})$ be a word map on $G$. Write $\mu_{G,w}(1)$ for the probability that $w(\overline{x})=1$ when $\overline{x}$ is chosen uniformly from $G^{|\overline{x}|}$. **Amit's conjecture.** For every such word map,

$$
\mu_{G,w}(1)\geq \frac{1}{|G|},
$$

i.e. the equation $w(\overline{x})=1$ has at least $|G|^{|\overline{x}|-1}$ solutions. This generalizes the preceding result for equations of the form $w(\overline{x})=c(\overline{x})$ with $c$ in the derived subgroup of the free group over $G$; its status is not resolved in the supplied source context.
record.source_name: William Cocke and Meng-Che "Turbo" Ho, “The Probability Distribution of Word Maps on Finite Groups”, arXiv:1807.07111 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.07111

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2018).

record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the no-spin Hartree–Fock minimisation problem
record.statement: Let $w$ be a positive radial non-increasing function. For density $\rho\geq 0$ and temperature $T\geq 0$, let $E_{\textnormal{no-spin}}^{\rm HF}(\rho,T)$ denote the no-spin Hartree–Fock minimisation problem. **Uniqueness for the no-spin problem.** The minimisation problem $E_{\textnormal{no-spin}}^{\rm HF}(\rho,T)$ admits a unique minimiser for every $\rho,T\geq 0$. This conjecture would rule out non-uniqueness at fixed density in the no-spin model, although non-uniqueness at fixed chemical potential may still occur and is relevant to possible spin-symmetry breaking.
record.source_name: David Gontier and Mathieu Lewin, “Spin symmetry breaking in the translation-invariant Hartree-Fock electron gas”, arXiv:1812.07679 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.07679

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2018).

record.title: Sharp phase transition for Hamilton cycles and near perfect matchings in the KPKVB model
record.statement:
Let $G(n;\alpha,
u)$ denote the KPKVB random graph, where $n$ is the number of vertices, $\alpha$ controls the radial distribution, and $
u$ controls the angular range. A **near perfect matching** is a matching covering all but at most one vertex. For $0<\alpha<1/2$, the model exhibits a phase transition in $
u$. **Sharp phase-transition conjecture.** For every $0<\alpha<1/2$ there exists a critical $
u_c=
u_c(\alpha)>0$ such that, when $
u<
u_c$, a.a.s. $G(n;\alpha,
u)$ has no near perfect matching, whereas, if $
u>
u_c$, a.a.s. $G(n;\alpha,
u)$ has a Hamilton cycle. The theorem preceding this conjecture establishes possibly different lower and upper thresholds, so the conjecture asserts that the dependence on $
u$ is sharp and that these thresholds coincide.
record.source_name: Nikolaos Fountoulakis, Dieter Mitsche, Tobias Müller and Markus Schepers, “Hamilton cycles and perfect matchings in the KPKVB model”, arXiv:1901.09175 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.09175

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

record.title: Infinitude of Fibonacci gap fibers
record.statement:
For a positive integer $\ell$ and an integer $m$, let

$$
D_\ell(m)=\{n:\exists k\geq 1\text{ such that }n=d_k,\ d_{k+\ell}-n=m\},
$$

and define $U_\ell(m)$ analogously. **Infinitude conjecture for gap fibers.** For every $m\in D_\ell$,

$$
|D_\ell(m)|=\infty.
$$

The conjecture expresses the expectation that every admissible down-gap occurs infinitely often; the source motivates it by a stronger positive-density suspicion, but leaves the stated infinitude claim open.
record.source_name: Fan Chung, Ron Graham and Sam Spiro, “Slow Fibonacci Walks”, arXiv:1903.08274 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.08274

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2019). “Perhaps the most important open problem is the following.”

record.title: Stabilization bound for standard skew tableaux
record.statement: A standard skew tableau has rows whose sizes weakly decrease from top to bottom; write $b$ for the number of rows and let $\stab$ denote its stabilization time, the least $k$ at which the tableau stabilization process becomes stable. **Stabilization bound conjecture.** Every standard skew tableau with $b$ rows and decreasing row sizes stabilizes at $b$. The paper verifies this for all standard skew tableaux of size at most $7$ and reports random searches without counterexamples. The bound is known to be tight for skew tableaux with constant row vectors, but the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Connor Ahlbach, “Tableau Stabilization and Rectangular Tableaux Fixed by Promotion Powers”, arXiv:1907.00105 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00105

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Missing-digit Cantor sets and Liouville numbers product-dimension conjecture
record.statement:
Let $b\geq 3$ and let $W\subseteq\{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}$. Define the missing-digit Cantor set

$$
C_{b,W}=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}a_i b^{-i}:a_i\in W\right\},
$$

and let $\mathscr{L}$ denote the set of Liouville numbers. For $n\geq 3$, **the missing-digit product-dimension conjecture.**

$$
\dim\bigl((\mathscr{L}\cap C_{b,W})^n\bigr)=(n-1)\dim(C_{b,W})=\frac{(n-1)\log|W|}{\log b}.
$$

The case $n=2$ is established in the surrounding discussion, while the argument given there does not extend to more factors. The conjecture predicts the corresponding Hausdorff dimension for every higher Cartesian power.
record.source_name: Johannes Schleischitz, “Metric results on sumsets and Cartesian products of classes of Diophantine sets”, arXiv:2002.08228 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08228

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

record.title: Strong synchronisation of alternating-group descent enumerators
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}_n$ be the alternating group in $\mathfrak{S}_n$, and let $A_{n,k}^+$ and $A_{n,k}^-$ denote the numbers of permutations with $k$ descents in $\mathcal{A}_n$ and $\mathfrak{S}_n\setminus\mathcal{A}_n$, respectively. Two sequences are **strongly synchronised** when each corresponding pair of terms satisfies the synchronisation inequalities defining this relation.

**Strong-synchronisation conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, the sequences $(A_{n,k}^+)_{k=0}^{n-1}$ and $(A_{n,k}^-)_{k=0}^{n-1}$ are strongly synchronised.

This conjecture would imply log-concavity of both descent enumerator sequences. The surrounding discussion also relates it to conjectures on real-rootedness of the alternating-group descent polynomials, but no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Hiranya Kishore Dey, “Log-concavity of the Excedance Enumerators in positive elements of Type A and Type B Coxeter Groups”, arXiv:2009.10655 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.10655

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

record.title: The linkedness conjecture for simple polytopes
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a **simple $d$-polytope**, meaning a $d$-dimensional polytope in which every vertex is incident to exactly $d$ edges. A polytope is $k$-linked when its graph is $k$-linked, namely, when every collection of $k$ pairwise disjoint pairs of vertices can be joined by pairwise vertex-disjoint paths. **Simple-polytope linkedness conjecture.** Every simple $d$-polytope is

$$
\floor{d/2}
$$

-linked for $d\geqslant 2$. The analogous assertion for arbitrary $d$-polytopes is false, while no counterexamples are known among simple polytopes; the conjecture asks whether simplicity guarantees the expected linkedness.
record.source_name: Leif K. Jorgensen, Guillermo Pineda-Villavicencio and Julien Ugon, “Linkedness of Cartesian products of complete graphs”, arXiv:2012.05576 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.05576

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: Partitioned configuration conjecture for complete bipartite subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $(\mathcal P,\mathcal H)$ be a point-hyperplane configuration in $\mathbb R^d$. A **not-necessarily-parallel $k$-partition** is a partition

$$
\mathcal H=\mathcal H_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup\mathcal H_\ell
$$

into blocks of size at most $k$ such that every point $p\in\mathcal P$ is incident to at least one hyperplane in every block.

**Partitioned configuration conjecture.** For every fixed integer $k>1$, every such configuration satisfies

$$
\operatorname{rs}(\mathcal P,\mathcal H) \geq mn\cdot 2^{-\operatorname{polylog}(d)}.
$$

This is presented as a relaxation of the parallel-partition conjecture. The source does not state that it is equivalent to the log-rank conjecture or provide a resolution, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Noah Singer and Madhu Sudan, “Point-hyperplane incidence geometry and the log-rank conjecture”, arXiv:2101.09592 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.09592

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2021). “This conjecture is a central and notorious open question in communication complexity.”

record.title: The small-cube conjecture for transitive sets
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite transitive subset of the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^d$ or $\mathbb{C}^d$. A unitary basis $L$ is a basis whose vectors are orthonormal with respect to the relevant real or complex inner product. Write $\langle \mathbf{v},\mathbf{x}\rangle$ for the inner product.

**Small-cube conjecture.** There is a unitary basis $L$ such that

$$
\sup_{\mathbf{x}\in X,\mathbf{v}\in L}|\langle \mathbf{v},\mathbf{x}\rangle|\lesssim \frac{1}{\sqrt{\log d}}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a coordinate system in which every point of every finite transitive set has uniformly small coordinates. The source presents it as a closely related conjecture; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Ashwin Sah, Mehtaab Sawhney and Yufei Zhao, “The cylindrical width of transitive sets”, arXiv:2101.11207 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.11207

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2021). “The following counterintuitive fact was conjectured by the third author and proved by Green .”

record.title: The directed-cycle fractalizer conjecture
record.statement: For a directed cycle $\vec{C}_k$, call a directed graph a **fractalizer** if its extremal induced-copy density is attained by iterated balanced blow-ups of $\vec{C}_k$. **Directed-cycle fractalizer conjecture.** For all $k\geq 4$, $\vec{C}_k$ is a fractalizer. The paper proves that $\vec{C}_5$ is a fractalizer and reports that related unpublished work establishes the corresponding property for $\vec{C}_4$ in a weaker stated form; the assertion for every $k\geq4$ remains open.
record.source_name: Bernard Lidický, Connor Mattes and Florian Pfender, “C_5 is almost a fractalizer”, arXiv:2102.06773 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.06773

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

record.title: Hereditary chromatic recurrence inside density-recurrent sets
record.statement: Let $S\subseteq\mathbb Z$ be a set of density recurrence, meaning that for every subset $A$ of a suitable positive upper density, $(A-A)\cap S\neq\varnothing$. **Hereditary recurrence conjecture.** There exists a set $S'\subseteq S$ such that $S'$ is a set of chromatic recurrence and is not a set of density recurrence. This conjecture concerns whether every density-recurrent set contains a chromatically recurrent subset that loses density recurrence; the source explicitly presents it as an open question related to the paper's results.
record.source_name: John T. Griesmer, “Separating topological recurrence from measurable recurrence: exposition and extension of Kriz's example”, arXiv:2108.01642 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01642

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

record.title: Full pattern support conjecture for skew Brownian permutons
record.statement:
Let $\bm \mu_{\rho,q}$ be a skew Brownian permuton with parameters $(\rho,q)\in(-1,1)\times(0,1)$. For $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, let $\pi$ be a permutation pattern of size $k$, and let $\operatorname{Perm}_k(\bm \mu_{\rho,q})$ be the permutation induced by $k$ independent points sampled from $\bm \mu_{\rho,q}$. **Full pattern support conjecture.** For all $(\rho,q)\in(-1,1)\times(0,1)$, all $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, and every pattern $\pi$ of size $k$,

$$
\mathbb{P}(\operatorname{Perm}_k(\bm \mu_{\rho,q})=\pi)>0.
$$

This asserts that every finite permutation pattern has positive probability for interior parameter values. The source presents it as an intuition-based statement; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Jacopo Borga, “The skew Brownian permuton: a new universality class for random constrained permutations”, arXiv:2112.00156 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.00156

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2021). “In this final section of the introduction, we collect a list of open questions and problems that we plan to address in future research projects.”

record.title: Conjecture relating normalized single-hypergraph Turán densities across uniformities
record.statement:
For an integer $r\geq 2$, let $\Pi_{1}^{(r)}$ denote the set of Turán densities of single $r$-graphs. **The normalized Turán-density conjecture.** If

$$
c\cdot\frac{r!}{r^r}
$$

is in $\Pi_{1}^{(r)}$ for $r\geq 2$, then

$$
c\cdot\frac{p!}{p^p}
$$

is in $\Pi_{1}^{(p)}$ for every integer $p\geq r$. The conjecture is proposed as a mechanism that would imply the existence of an $r$-graph with irrational Turán density; the source does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Zilong Yan and Yuejian Peng, “An irrational Lagrangian density of a single hypergraph”, arXiv:2112.14935 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.14935

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2021). “Baber and Talbot , and Pikhurko disproved this conjecture by showing that there is an irrational number in $\Pi_{3}^{(3)}$ and $\Pi_{fin}^{(3)}$, respectively.”

record.title: Steiner triple system hitting-time conjecture
record.statement: Let $n\equiv 1,3 \pmod 6$, and let $T_1,T_2,\ldots$ be a uniformly random ordering of the triples in $\binom{[n]}{3}$. **Steiner triple system hitting-time conjecture.** With high probability, the first prefix $T_1,\ldots,T_k$ that covers every $2$-edge at least once contains a Steiner triple system. The conjecture is the corresponding hitting-time version of the proposed sharp threshold and is presented by the source as an open direction.
record.source_name: Ashwin Sah, Mehtaab Sawhney and Michael Simkin, “Threshold for Steiner triple systems”, arXiv:2204.03964 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.03964

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: The pyramidal and quasi-pyramidal growth conjectures for polytopes
record.statement: Let $\mathbf{POL}$ be the poset of polytopes, let $\underset{\Delta}{\le}$ denote pyramidal growth, and let $\underset{\mathbf q}{\le}$ denote quasi-pyramidal growth. For a quasi-pyramidal pair $P\underset{\mathbf q}{\le}Q$, let $\delta(P,Q)$ be its quasi-pyramidal defect. **Pyramidal growth conjecture.** (a) Pyramidal growth is not the inclusion order in $\mathbf{POL}(4)$. (b) For every $d$, quasi-pyramidal growth is the inclusion order in $\mathbf{POL}(d)$ and $\delta(P,Q)=0$ for any polytopes $P\subset Q$. The source says these claims are expected in parallel with the cone-poset conjecture; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Joseph Gubeladze, “Normal polytopes: between discrete, continuous, and random”, arXiv:2206.06306 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.06306

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: Lower bound for quasirandom-forcing linear combinations
record.statement: A linear combination of permutation patterns is **quasirandom-forcing** if it has the quasirandomness-forcing property studied in the paper. The number of terms means the number of permutation patterns appearing in the linear combination, and coefficients may be positive or negative. **Lower-bound conjecture.** There are no quasirandom-forcing linear combinations with fewer than six terms, even if negative coefficients are allowed. The paper proves the corresponding result for positive coefficients, while the extension to arbitrary coefficients remains open because vanishing covers and possible infinite families must be analyzed.
record.source_name: Gabriel Crudele, Peter Dukes and Jonathan A. Noel, “Six Permutation Patterns Force Quasirandomness”, arXiv:2303.04776 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.04776

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

record.title: Bipartite-graph density dichotomy conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a bipartite graph. For a graph $G$, write $d(G)$ for its average degree. **Bipartite-graph density dichotomy conjecture.** For every bipartite graph $H$, there is a constant $C_H$ such that, for every integer $s\geq 1$ and every $H$-free graph $G$ with

$$
d(G)\geq s^{C_H},
$$

either $G$ contains a copy of $K_{s,s}$, or $G$ has an induced subgraph $G'\subset G$ with $d(G')\geq s$ that contains no $4$-cycles. This would give a polynomial density alternative for $H$-free graphs, separating large balanced bicliques from dense induced $C_4$-free subgraphs.
record.source_name: António Girão and Zach Hunter, “Induced subdivisions in K_s,s-free graphs with polynomial average degree”, arXiv:2310.18452 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18452

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: Low-moment star graph spectral-gap conjecture
record.statement:
For a star graph $G_{\star}$ with $n_{\star}$ vertices, let $\Delta(G_{\star},n_{\star},k)$ denote the spectral gap of its Hamiltonian at moment $k$. **Low-moment star graph conjecture.** The second- and third-moment star graph gaps satisfy

$$
\Delta(G_{\star},n_{\star},k)>\frac{1}{2}
$$

for $k=2$ and $k=3$. This conjecture would provide the spectral-gap input needed to show that local random quantum circuits form approximate designs on arbitrary connected graphs; the paper presents numerical and analytic evidence, but no proof for all $n_{\star}$.
record.source_name: Shivan Mittal and Nicholas Hunter-Jones, “Local random quantum circuits form approximate designs on arbitrary architectures”, arXiv:2310.19355 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19355

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).
